title: ABC-Sampling: An Effective Method for Dealing with Fraud Detection in Financial Imbalanced Datasets
authors: Darwish, S. M.; Abdelkader, H. M.; Alsharif, S. H.
tldr: Proposes ABC-Sampling, a hybrid sampling method combining SMOTE with Artificial Bee Colony optimization (ABC) to address class imbalance for fraud detection in financial datasets.
problem_and_motivation: Fraud detection in financial transactions faces severe class imbalance (fraud often <1% of transactions), causing ML classifiers to be biased toward the majority class and miss fraudulent cases. Existing sampling methods struggle with high-dimensional financial data.
approach: Proposed ABC-Sampling: uses Artificial Bee Colony algorithm to intelligently select which synthetic samples to generate for the minority class.
ABC optimization balances exploration and exploitation in sample generation, avoiding noisy/overlapping synthetic samples that SMOTE alone produces.
Applied ABC-Sampling to preprocess three financial fraud datasets before training ML classifiers.
Compared against SMOTE, ADASYN, Borderline-SMOTE, and hybrid variants using RF, XGBoost, and MLP classifiers.
Evaluated using precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC, and G-mean metrics.
findings: num: ABC-Sampling improved F1-score by 8.2% over SMOTE and 12.4% over ADASYN across all classifiers.
num: XGBoost with ABC-Sampling achieved 97.3% AUC-ROC and 0.94 F1-score on the largest dataset.
ABC-Sampling generates fewer but higher quality synthetic samples compared to SMOTE.
ABC-Sampling with RF achieved best recall (96.8%) for fraud class detection.
Hybrid sampling with intelligent selection outperforms both oversampling (SMOTE) and undersampling approaches individually.

Hybrid sampling using ABC to intelligently select synthetic minority samples for class imbalance handling.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Proposes a novel hybrid sampling method (ABC-Sampling) that combines SMOTE with Artificial Bee Colony optimization for intelligent sample generation in imbalanced fraud detection. The approach addresses the quality vs. quantity trade-off in synthetic sampling by using ABC to select informative synthetic instances. Demonstrates consistent improvements over standard sampling methods across multiple datasets and classifiers.
directly_justifies: Class imbalance is a critical challenge for ML-based fraud detection.
ABC optimization improves synthetic sample quality over standard SMOTE.
Hybrid sampling with intelligent selection outperforms individual oversampling methods.
limits: Tested on only three datasets; broader generalization unestablished. [acknowledged]
ABC-Sampling adds computational overhead for sample selection. [unacknowledged]
No XAI mechanism provided for fraud classification decisions. [unacknowledged]
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was performed. Domains 8.A (fraud detection) and 14.A (ML approaches) were flagged as highly relevant because the paper proposes a novel sampling algorithm for fraud detection in financial datasets. Domains 1-7, 9-13, 14.B were rejected as the paper focuses purely on the sampling component of fraud detection ML pipelines without covering user aspects, other PFMS tasks, or explainability.

limitations: Computational cost of ABC optimization not analyzed. [unacknowledged]
